# These settings are mainly for the wrapper scripts around aide,
# such as aideinit and dailyaidecheck

# Main configuration file
CONFIG="/etc/aide/aide.conf"

# Set this to no to disable daily aide runs
#CRON_DAILY_RUN=yes

# The following variables control the sending of e-mail reports from
# the daily aide check. See /usr/share/doc/aide-common/README.Debian
# for detailed documentaton. Commented out settings are the default.
#FQDN=
#MAILSUBJ="Daily AIDE report for $FQDN"
#MAILTO=root
#MAILCMD=
#MAILWIDTH=990

# Set this to yes to suppress mailings when no changes have been
# detected during the AIDE run and no error output was given.
#QUIETREPORTS=no

# Set this to yes to suppress mailings under all circumstances
# This option implies QUIETREPORTS=yes
#SILENTREPORTS=no

# Set this to no if you have figlet installed but do not want figlet
# output in your daily aide check mail
#FIGLET=yes

# This parameter defines which AIDE command to run from the daily aide check.
# Sensible values are "update" and "check".
# Default is "check", ensuring backwards compatibility.
# Since "update" does not take any longer, it is recommended to use "update",
# so that a new database is created every day. The new database needs to be
# manually copied over the current one, though.
COMMAND=update

# This parameter defines what to do with a new database created by
# COMMAND=update. It is ignored if COMMAND!=update.
# no: Do not copy new database to old database. This is the default.
# yes: Copy new database to old database. This means that changes to the
#   file system are only reported once. Possibly dangerous.
# ifnochange: Copy new database to old database if no changes have
#   been reported. This is needed for ANF/ARF to work reliably.
COPYNEWDB=no

# Set this to yes to truncate the detailed changes part in the mail. The full
# output will still be listed in the log file.
TRUNCATEDETAILS=no

# Set this to yes to suppress file changes by package and security
# updates from appearing in the e-mail report. Filtered file changes will
# still be listed in the log file. This option parses the /var/log/dpkg.log
# file and implies TRUNCATEDETAILS=yes
FILTERUPDATES=no

# Set this to yes to suppress file changes by package installations
# from appearing in the e-mail report. Filtered file changes will still
# be listed in the log file. This option parses the /var/log/dpkg.log file and
# implies TRUNCATEDETAILS=yes.
FILTERINSTALLATIONS=no

# This parameter defines how many lines to return per e-mail. Output longer
# than this value will be truncated in the e-mail sent out.
# Set value to "0" to disable this option.
LINES=1000

# This parameter gives a grep regular expression. If given, all output lines
# that _don't_ match the regexp are listed first in the script's output. This
# allows to easily remove noise from the AIDE report.
NOISE=""

# This parameter defines which options are given to aide in the daily
# aide check. The default is "-V4".
AIDEARGS=""

# Set this to a command that will be executed before the daily aide check
# exits. This can be used to postprocess the generated report.
# If the command is not in /sbin:/usr/sbin:/bin:/usr/bin (see PATH
# setting in the daily aide check), you need to give a fully qualified
# path. The script is executed before the aide lock is released.
# The hook is called with a single parameter meaning:
#    signal: The daily aide check was terminated by a signal
#    fatal: There was a fatal error
#    nolock: The lock could not be obtained
#    cantmovetmp: It was not possible to move away the temporary directory
#    cantcreatetmp: It was not possible to create the temporary directory
#    success: aide finished successfully and gave meaningful results
#    unknown: onexit was called with an illegal reason (should not happen)
# If the daily aide check aborted before the environment was fully set up,
# "early-" is prepended to the reason.
CRONEXITHOOK=""

# See documentation in aide.conf(5). To list the default compount

    outfile=$(grep -E "^[[:space:]]*database_out=file:" "${config}" | cut -d: -f2)
    [ -z "${outfile}" ] && outfile="/var/lib/aide/aide.db.new"
fi
if [ -z "${dbfile}" ]; then
    dbfile=$(grep -E "^[[:space:]]*database_in=file:" "${config}" | cut -d: -f2)
    [ -z "${dbfile}" ] && dbfile="/var/lib/aide/aide.db"
fi

if [ -f "${outfile}" ]; then
    if [ $opt_y -eq 0 ]; then
        printf "Overwrite existing %s [Yn]? " "${outfile}"
        read yn
        case "$yn" in
            [Nn]*)
            exit 0
            ;;
        esac
    fi
fi

extraflags=""

run_aideinit() {
    if command -v capsh >/dev/null; then
        capsh --caps="cap_dac_read_search,cap_audit_write+eip cap_setpcap,cap_setuid,cap_setgid+ep" --keep=1 --user=_aide --addamb=cap_dac_read_search,cap_audit_write -- \
            -c "aide --config=${config} --init $extraflags $@ >/var/log/aide/aideinit.log 2>/var/log/aide/aideinit.errors"
        RET=$?
    else
        aide --config="${config}" --init ${extraflags} $@ >/var/log/aide/aideinit.log 2>/var/log/aide/aideinit.errors

    fi
    printf "AIDE --init return code %d\\n" "${RET}" >> /var/log/aide/aideinit.log
    if [ "$RET" != "0" ]; then
       printf "AIDE --init return code %d\\n" "${RET}" >> /var/log/aide/aideinit.errors
    fi
    return $RET
}

aideinit_background() {

--- package README scheduling notes ---
120-^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
121-Starting with aide 0.18, the Debian packages do create a system user
122-_aide on installation and try hard to run aide as that user. This
123:needs either the system having systemd as pid 1 or capsh(1) from the
124-libcap2-bin package installed.  If neither is the case, aide runs as
125-root. A non-root aide is augmented with the cap_dac_read_search
126-capability which allows the non-root user to read anywhere.
127-
128:The daily aide cron job running as non-root on a systemd system cannot
129-send out mail via the traditional /usr/lib/sendmail interface since
130:the capability-related systemd unit also disabled suid which is needed
131-for the MTA to function. This affects both mailx and bsd-mailx.
132:Non-root aide on systemd systems can only send out mail if s-nail is
133-installed, which in turn relies on a local MTA to listen for s-nail's
134-SMTP connections.
135-
136-This affects both new installations and upgraded installations.
137-See below for details.
138-
139-A significant part of the shell scripts that surround the aide calls
140-in Debian will still run as root.  Patches accepted.
141-
142:The non-systemd code paths are badly tested. Please expect breakage
143-and send patches. We appreciate your help here.
144-
145-
146-the daily AIDE check
147-^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
148-Main work of the aide package happens in a daily job. On a system
149:using systemd, it's a system timer running between 0200 and 0400. On a
150:system that is not using systemd, the same job is invoked via
151:cron.daily.
152-
153-Logging
154--------
155-The daily job invokes aide, instructs aide to write the report to a
156-temporary file. Standard error is captured to a temporary file as
157-well. The actual command which is invoked is controlled by the COMMAND
158-variable in /etc/default/aide, and additional parameters can be passed
159-in via AIDEARGS in /etc/default/aide. Standard output eventually ends
--
230-To send out mail reports, the daily aide check either uses s-nail or
231-mail(1) (such as the executable provided by bsd-mailx).  If neither is
232-installed, a warning is given on stderr (this ends up in the Journal
233:if systemd is used or is sent via e-mail by the cron daemon).  Set
234-SILENTREPORTS=yes to confirm that you really want the daily aide check
235-to be silent.  Logs are written in either case.
236-
237-S-nail is the tool preferred by the script to send out the message via
238-SMTP to localhost.  A working MTA is expected on localhost.  An
239-unqualified recipient address is qualified with the contents of
240-/etc/mailname to make it acceptable over SMTP.
241-
242-If s-nail is not installed, and the daily cron job is running as
243:non-root under systemd, it will log a message to the journal and the
244:log file and not send mail. On a non-systemd system, it will use
245-mail(1) to send the message.  This is done this way because most
246-implementations of mail(1) use /usr/lib/sendmail to deliver the
247-outgoing message. /usr/lib/sendmail is suid root with some MTAs, and
248-this way of privilege escalation is not available when the daily aide
249:job is invoked a non-root user by systemd.
250-
251-The daily aide check will automatically select the method of sending
252-mail according to the rules documented above.  The variable MAILCMD in
253-/etc/default/aide can be used to override these rules.  If you know
254-that your mail(1) works in a scenario where the automatism refuses to
255-use mail(1), setting MAILCMD to the path to mail(1) manually will force
256-the script to use mail(1).  If you need more flexibility and/or would
257-prefer to have additional methods of delivering the report supported

sudo systemctl start dailyaidecheck.service
printf 'service_result='; systemctl show dailyaidecheck.service -p Result --value
printf 'service_exit_status='; systemctl show dailyaidecheck.service -p ExecMainStatus --value
printf 'timer_enabled='; systemctl is-enabled dailyaidecheck.timer
printf 'timer_active='; systemctl is-active dailyaidecheck.timer
printf '%s\n' '--- latest daily report ---'
sudo grep -E 'AIDE found|Number of entries|Start timestamp|End timestamp' /var/log/aide/aide.log | tail -n 10
printf '%s\n' '--- recent service journal ---'
sudo journalctl -u dailyaidecheck.service -n 12 --no-pager

command:
set -eu
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf 'database_sha256='; sudo sha256sum /var/lib/aide/aide.db | awk '{print $1}'
printf 'database_bytes='; sudo stat -c '%s' /var/lib/aide/aide.db
printf 'timer_enabled='; systemctl is-enabled dailyaidecheck.timer
printf 'timer_active='; systemctl is-active dailyaidecheck.timer
sudo aide --config=/etc/aide/aide-etc.conf --check > /tmp/aide-pre-reboot.log 2>&1
rc=$?
grep -E 'AIDE found|Number of entries' /tmp/aide-pre-reboot.log
printf 'pre_reboot_check_exit=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"
